prerequisites: Analysis of the mechanical behavior of materials and structures (RDM, solid mechanics) (IGENI-EC0222, IGENI-EC0321, IGENI-EC0521)

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to select and implement the most appropriate kinematic, thermal and NDT field measurement techniques for industrial and laboratory applications, from various innovative, high-performance techniques.
They will also be able to use and analyse the results obtained to identify the mechanical behaviour of materials and structures.
Master the fundamentals and key features of optical methods for non-contact measurement of kinematic and thermal fields to analyse the behaviour of materials and structures.
Master the fundamentals and key features of optical methods for defect detection and material health of materials and structures.
Understand the main methods for inverse identification of mechanical behaviour models.
Apply new experimental methods to identify the mechanical behaviour or material health of materials and structures.

syllabus_topics: New optical methods for studying the behaviour of materials and structures
Methods for measuring surface displacements and deformations
Methods for measuring relief, volume, out-of-plane displacements and deformations
Measurement of thermal fields by IR thermography
Review of basic heat transfer concepts
Thermal radiation: description of the phenomenon, thermal laws, black and real bodies
Principles of thermal measurement: existing devices, IRT acquisition principles and procedures, factors influencing measurement
Applications illustrated through laboratory activities: NDT, damage monitoring, manufacturing process monitoring
Using field measurements to identify behaviour laws
Mechanical behaviour laws: reminders and definition of requirements
Parametric identification and recalibration of finite element numerical models (FEMU)
